content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is drafted and passes all quality checks. Per our Spec-Driven workflow, **this is the first gate** — please review before we plan anything. No code will be written yet.

- **Spec:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- **Quality checklist:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md` (all items pass)

## Spec summary for your review

**What it covers (prioritized user journeys):**
1. **P1 — Save a bookmark:** enter an address, it's stored and listed; auto-derives a title if none given; rejects invalid addresses. *(This alone is a working MVP.)*
2. **P2 — Browse & find:** list everything, search by title/address, open a bookmark in a new tab, clear empty-state message.
3. **P3 — Organize with tags:** apply tags, filter to one tag, clear the filter.
4. **P3 — Edit & delete:** correct details; delete with a confirmation step.

**12 functional requirements**, **2 entities** (Bookmark, Tag), and **5 measurable success criteria** (e.g. save a bookmark in under 30s; find one in a 100+ collection in under 10s; 100% persistence across restarts).

## Key assumptions I made — please confirm or correct these

These most affect scope, so they're the main things to react to at this gate:

| # | Assumption | If you disagree |
|---|-----------|-----------------|
| 1 | **Single user, personal use — no sign-in / accounts** | Say so if it needs multiple users or shared collections (bigger scope) |
| 2 | **Browser-based web app** | Tell me if you meant a browser extension, mobile, or desktop app |
| 3 | **Organize by flexible tags** (a bookmark can have several) | Say if you'd prefer strict folders instead |
| 4 | **Auto-fetches page titles**, best-effort, falls back to the address | Confirm if that's wanted or unnecessary |

**How to proceed:**
- If this looks right, say **approve** and I'll move to the **plan** gate (`speckit-plan`).
- If anything's off, tell me what to change and I'll update the spec first — we route changes through the spec, not the code.
- If you'd like, I can also run a structured **clarify** pass (`speckit-clarify`) to tighten any ambiguous points before planning.

What would you like to adjust, or shall I proceed to planning?

Please run the clarify pass before planning. The four main assumptions are broadly right: this is a private, single-user browser app, and I prefer flexible tags rather than folders.

I do want several corrections and additions:

- When I save a page, please try to collect its title, description, site icon, and preview image—not only its title. I should be able to adjust the title and description before saving and later.
- Saving the same address again should not create a duplicate. It should take me to the existing bookmark so I can edit it.
- A bookmark should also support a personal note, including formatted Markdown.
- The list should emphasize readability and show the title, description, tags, and site icon. Search should cover the title, description, note, and address without caring about capitalization.
- I want richer searching: `#tag`, quoted exact phrases, and combinations such as AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.
- I need a “read later” state, with a separate unread view and a way to mark items read.
- Please include sorting and selecting bookmarks for bulk changes, including changing tags, read status, archiving, and deleting. Applying an action to all matching results should respect the current search or filter.
- Archiving should be reversible and separate from deleting. Archived items should have their own view and stay out of the normal list and ordinary searches.
- I’d like saved reusable filters that can combine a search with included and excluded tags.
- Please preserve a local copy of a saved page, using the original PDF when the link is a PDF, and offer an Internet Archive copy as well.
- I also need bookmark import and export in the common browser bookmark HTML format, preserving titles, tags, and saved dates.
- Finally, include a few personal display preferences such as default sorting, how many items are shown, and text size.

Once those points and their important edge cases are made clear in the specification, I’ll review it again before planning.

content:
Prerequisites resolved. I ran the ambiguity scan against the updated spec. Most categories are Clear, but a handful of high-impact decisions are still marked "to be confirmed" in the spec. I'll ask them one at a time (up to 5). You can reply with a letter, say "yes"/"recommended" to accept my pick, or give your own short answer.

---

**Question:** When deciding whether an address is a duplicate, how aggressively should the app treat near-identical addresses as "the same page"?

**Why it matters:** This sets when saving re-opens an existing bookmark versus creating a new one — too loose merges genuinely different pages, too strict lets duplicates slip in. It also defines the acceptance test for SC-004 (zero duplicates).

**Recommended:** Option B — matches how people expect duplicates to be caught (a trailing slash or `utm_` tracking tag shouldn't count as a new page) while keeping distinct paths and meaningful query parameters separate.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Exact match only — the address must be character-for-character identical |
| B | Normalize lightly — ignore scheme (http/https), a `www.` prefix, host capitalization, a trailing slash, and common tracking parameters (e.g. `utm_*`, `fbclid`); keep the path and other query parameters significant |
| C | Aggressive — also drop all query parameters and `#fragments`, so only host + path matter |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
B — use the recommended light normalization. Distinct paths and meaningful query parameters should remain separate.
relayed: B — use the recommended light normalization. Distinct paths and meaningful query parameters should remain separate.
raw_content: B — use the recommended light normalization. Distinct paths and meaningful query parameters should remain separate.

content:
Now Q2:

**Question:** When you save a new bookmark, what should its read state be by default?

**Why it matters:** This decides whether the unread view acts as an inbox of everything you save (so nothing is missed) or only holds items you deliberately flag. It sets the expected behavior for US5's acceptance test.

**Recommended:** Option A — a bookmarking tool's read-later queue is most useful when every newly saved item lands in "unread" automatically and you clear it as you go; this matches the workflow you described.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Every newly saved bookmark starts as **unread** (the unread view is an inbox of all new saves) |
| B | New bookmarks start as **read**; the user explicitly marks items "to read" when they want them queued |
| C | Ask/choose per save (a toggle at save time, defaulting to unread) |

You can reply with the option letter, accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
B — new bookmarks should start as read. I only want items in the unread view when I deliberately mark them “read later.”
relayed: B — new bookmarks should start as read. I only want items in the unread view when I deliberately mark them “read later.”
raw_content: B — new bookmarks should start as read. I only want items in the unread view when I deliberately mark them “read later.”

content:
Now Q3:

**Question:** When an import contains an address you've already saved, what should happen to the existing bookmark?

**Why it matters:** This defines the outcome of re-importing or merging collections (FR-031, SC-008) — whether your existing tags/notes are protected, enriched, or overwritten.

**Recommended:** Option B — merging non-destructively (add any new tags from the file, keep the earliest saved date, and never overwrite a note/description you've already written) preserves your work while still absorbing useful data from the import.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | **Skip** — leave the existing bookmark untouched; ignore the incoming duplicate entirely |
| B | **Merge non-destructively** — union the tags, keep the earliest saved date, and preserve existing title/description/note (only fill fields that are currently empty) |
| C | **Overwrite** — replace the existing bookmark's fields with the imported values |

You can reply with the option letter, accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
B — merge non-destructively. Preserve what I’ve already written, add new tags, fill only empty fields, and keep the earliest saved date.
relayed: B — merge non-destructively. Preserve what I’ve already written, add new tags, fill only empty fields, and keep the earliest saved date.
raw_content: B — merge non-destructively. Preserve what I’ve already written, add new tags, fill only empty fields, and keep the earliest saved date.

content:
Now Q4:

**Question:** What should the preserved local copy of a saved page actually contain?

**Why it matters:** This drives how much storage the app uses and how faithful the offline copy is — a full-fidelity capture with images can be large, while a readable-text snapshot stays lightweight. It sets the acceptance test for US12/FR-025.

**Recommended:** Option B — a self-contained readable snapshot (the article text and essential inline images folded into a single saved file) survives link rot and stays legible offline without the storage cost and fragility of capturing every asset on the page. PDFs are always kept as the original file regardless of this choice.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | **Readable text only** — extract the main article text (and the preview image); smallest storage, loses page layout |
| B | **Self-contained readable snapshot** — main content plus its essential inline images embedded in one saved file; legible offline, moderate size |
| C | **Full-page capture** — the complete page with all assets/styling as it appeared; highest fidelity, largest storage, more capture failures |

You can reply with the option letter, accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
C — I want a full-page copy that preserves the page’s appearance and content in a single file. For PDF links, keep the original PDF instead.
relayed: C — I want a full-page copy that preserves the page’s appearance and content in a single file. For PDF links, keep the original PDF instead.
raw_content: C — I want a full-page copy that preserves the page’s appearance and content in a single file. For PDF links, keep the original PDF instead.

content:
Now Q5 (final):

**Question:** The standard browser bookmark HTML format has no official field for tags — how should the app carry tags through import and export?

**Why it matters:** This determines whether your tags survive a round-trip (SC-008 requires 100% tag preservation) and how well they interoperate with other tools that read the same file.

**Recommended:** Option A — the widely-used `TAGS="..."` attribute (used by Firefox, Pocket, Delicious-style exports) keeps a flat tag set intact on round-trip and is the closest thing to a de-facto standard, which fits your flexible-tag model better than nesting folders.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Use the common `TAGS="tag1,tag2"` attribute on each bookmark entry (de-facto convention; flat tags preserved exactly) |
| B | Map each tag to a bookmark **folder** (most portable to browsers, but a multi-tag bookmark must be duplicated across folders, and round-trip can create duplicates) |
| C | Both — write the `TAGS` attribute *and* mirror tags as folders for maximum interoperability |

You can reply with the option letter, accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
A — use the common `TAGS` attribute so multiple tags survive import and export without creating duplicate bookmarks.
relayed: A — use the common `TAGS` attribute so multiple tags survive import and export without creating duplicate bookmarks.
raw_content: A — use the common `TAGS` attribute so multiple tags survive import and export without creating duplicate bookmarks.

The plan gate is ready for your review. Nothing has been implemented — these are design documents derived from the approved spec.

## Plan gate — artifacts for review

**Branch:** `001-bookmark-manager` · **Plan:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md`

| Artifact | What it covers |
|----------|----------------|
| `plan.md` | Architecture, tech context, constitution check, project structure |
| `research.md` | 12 resolved decisions (with rationale + alternatives) |
| `data-model.md` | 5 entities + FTS search index, fields, rules, relationships |
| `contracts/rest-api.md` | REST endpoints for every user story |
| `contracts/search-grammar.md` | The rich-search language (grammar, evaluation, errors) |
| `contracts/bookmark-html.md` | Import/export format + non-destructive merge rules |
| `quickstart.md` | Build/run/validate guide mapped to the success criteria |

## Key technical decisions (please react to these)

- **One Node.js/TypeScript service** (Express) that serves a **React/Vite** SPA and a REST API — a single `npm start` on `0.0.0.0:4000` for review.
- **SQLite** (better-sqlite3) with **FTS5** full-text search; preserved page copies stored as **files on disk**, not in the database.
- **Full-page copy = MHTML** captured via the pre-installed **Playwright + Chromium** (CDP snapshot); **PDF links keep the original PDF**. Size cap **25 MB** → oversize copies marked unavailable.
- **Rich search = a custom parser → boolean AST → SQLite** (needed because FTS5's own syntax can't express quoted-operators-as-literals or `#tag` semantics).
- **Markdown notes** rendered with markdown-it + **DOMPurify** sanitization (no active content).
- **Internet Archive** via the Wayback availability/save APIs — **best-effort**; if the review container has no outbound internet, live capture and Wayback degrade gracefully and I'll report that honestly rather than claim success.

## One thing worth flagging

Two capabilities depend on **outbound internet** inside the review container: live metadata/MHTML capture and Internet Archive lookups. The app is designed to degrade gracefully (bookmark still saves, copy marked unavailable), but full end-to-end verification of those two features may be limited at review time.

---

Everything is in place. No `.specify/extensions.yml`, so no `after_implement` hooks to dispatch.

## Implementation complete — ready for review

The full-scope Bookmark Manager is built, tested, and wired for review at **`http://maker:4000`**. The harness will start it via `.harness/app.json` (`npm start`). It's seeded with demo data so all views are populated.

### What was built (all 14 user stories)
A single Node/Express + TypeScript service serving a React SPA, SQLite storage, and Playwright/Chromium capture:
- **Save with metadata** (editable title/description/icon/preview) · **duplicate-free** saving via light URL normalization
- **Rich search** (`#tag`, `"phrases"`, `AND/OR/NOT`, parentheses, quoted-operators-as-literal) · sort · **read-later** · **archive** · **bulk actions** incl. "apply to all matching"
- **Tags** with reuse suggestions · **Markdown notes** (sanitized) · **saved filters** · **full-page MHTML/PDF copies** + Internet Archive · **import/export** (Netscape HTML, `TAGS` attribute) · **display preferences**

### Verification
- **21 automated tests pass** (Vitest): URL normalization, rich-search grammar incl. quoted operators, duplicate detection, import/merge round-trip (SC-008), bulk all-matching (SC-006), read-later/archive semantics
- **Perf (SC-002):** search over 2,000 bookmarks in **3–5ms**
- **E2E smoke passes** (Playwright): save → search → read-later → archive → export round-trip
- Manual API checks: invalid URL → 400, duplicate resolves to existing, malformed search → clear 400, SPA served, export emits `TAGS`

### Honest caveats (as approved)
- **External services are best-effort:** live metadata fetch, MHTML/PDF capture, and Internet Archive lookups need outbound internet. In the review container these degrade gracefully — the bookmark still saves and its local copy shows **"unavailable."** The seeded demo bookmarks were created offline, so they intentionally show local copy *unavailable* and fallback icons. Saving a fresh bookmark through the UI **will** attempt capture if the container has network.
- **Two tasks not fully completed** (marked in `tasks.md`): **T005** ESLint/Prettier tooling (deferred — doesn't affect build/test/run) and **T076** a full accessibility audit (partial — readable layout and working text-size are done; keyboard/contrast/ARIA audit deferred).

### The US1+US2 checkpoint
As you noted, the P1 save/duplicate flow is a reviewable checkpoint, **not** the finished release — the full P1–P4 scope is implemented here. When you open the app you can exercise everything: save a bookmark, try the rich search, mark items read-later, archive, create a saved filter, and import/export from **Settings**.
